Well-motivated approach leveraging occupancy measures as complete behavioral characterization, differentiating from prior work using proxy objectives

Thoughtfully designed cwPCA that addresses practical QD challenges: fitness weighting for high-performing policies, calibration for stable archive bounds, and geometry preservation via linear transformation
Comprehensive experimental validation across 6 environments with 5 baselines, 3 evaluation metrics, ablation studies, and robustness analysis to environmental changes
Consistent empirical gains: highest GT QD Score in 4/6 environments and strong robustness to dynamics changes (friction AUC 1429.66 vs 30.27 for RegularQD)
Clear presentation with good figures, detailed algorithms, and reproducibility-supporting appendices
weaknesses: Significant theory-practice gap: Theorem 1 assumes i.i.d. occupancy measure samples (φ^π) but implementation uses trajectory-based embeddings (ψ^π) without formal analysis of how this deviation affects theoretical guarantees
Fixed kernel bandwidth (σ = √(state_dim + action_dim)) lacks justification and no sensitivity analysis provided, yet significantly impacts behavior discrimination

Mixed empirical results across metrics: HalfCheetah achieves high diversity but low quality (low qVS=1.35 due to 'sliding' behaviors); Walker2d loses to Aurora on qVS metric, suggesting environment-dependent effectiveness

Unresolved practical limitations: acknowledged but not addressed include sample inefficiency in stochastic environments, scalability constraints from discretized QD archives, and lack of computational cost analysis vs baselines

Limited experimental scope: single domain (continuous control), weak baselines (SMERL and DvD-ES perform extremely poorly), no comparison against recent gradient-based QD methods (DQD, PGA-MAP-Elites, PPGA), no evaluation on image-based or discrete domains

Incomplete ablations: embedding/descriptor dimension ablations only on BipedalWalker; other hyperparameters (update schedule, kernel sensitivity, cwPCA weighting) unexplored; theorem bound tightness not empirically validated
GT QD Score evaluation potentially biased toward hand-crafted foot-contact descriptors, disadvantaging methods discovering different behavioral dimensions
Limited qualitative analysis of discovered behaviors; learned low-dimensional descriptors not interpreted (what do projections represent?); insufficient analysis of failures (Walker2d, HalfCheetah)
Incremental novelty: combines well-established techniques (RFF for MMD, standard PCA, existing CMA-MAE) rather than introducing fundamentally new concepts
Code availability not mentioned; implementation details (state normalization procedure) unclear; no wall-clock time comparisons with baselines

strengths: Solid theoretical contribution with Theorem 1 rigorously bounding RFF approximation of MMD between occupancy measures, with clear convergence guarantees in n and D
Well-motivated approach using occupancy measures as complete policy representations with proven one-to-one correspondence
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 6 environments with multiple baselines and three different evaluation metrics (GT QD, Vendi Score, qVS)
Thorough implementation details in appendices enabling reasonable reproducibility
Practical algorithm design with iterative refinement of descriptors and seamless integration with CMA-MAE
Robustness analysis under environmental perturbations (friction/mass changes) showing discovered policies generalize better
weaknesses: Critical theory-practice gap: Theorem 1 assumes i.i.d. samples from occupancy measures, but practical implementation (Eq. 6) uses weighted trajectory sums that violate assumptions; claim that ψ^π has 'same expectation' lacks rigorous proof and the weighted formulation fundamentally differs from theory

Inconsistent and mixed empirical results undermine claims: HalfCheetah shows Aurora superior (qVS 2.39 vs 1.35), Walker2d shows RegularQD superior (qVS 9.08 vs 7.22); method discovers low-performing 'sliding' behaviors in some domains

Problematic evaluation methodology: GT QD Score uses hand-crafted descriptors to evaluate a method designed to avoid them (circular evaluation); Vendi Score kernel is structurally similar to AutoQD's embeddings, potentially biasing evaluation

Limited technical novelty: Random Fourier Features for kernel approximation are well-established; occupancy measure use is natural but not novel; Calibrated Weighted PCA is straightforward; main contribution is incremental combination of existing techniques

Inadequate investigation of failure modes: HalfCheetah and Walker2d failures acknowledged but not deeply analyzed; paper provides no systematic understanding of when occupancy measure embeddings capture task-relevant behavioral distinctions

Hyperparameter sensitivity concerns: fixed kernel bandwidth with no principled selection method (acknowledged limitation), arbitrary update schedule without justification, Figure 5 shows mean objective quality degrades substantially with descriptor dimensionality (~120 point drop from 1-D to 4-D)

Scalability limitations not addressed: experiments use small networks (128 units, Toeplitz structure); paper acknowledges QD struggles with larger networks but provides no evidence AutoQD addresses this

Missing ablations and justifications: no comparison of cwPCA versus standard PCA or other dimensionality reduction methods; calibration step appears ad-hoc; why MMD/occupancy measures are better than alternative behavioral distance metrics unexplored
Statistical rigor concerns: only 3 random seeds used; some differences fall within error margins; no formal significance testing
Incomplete scope: only continuous control tested; image-based observations omitted despite being mentioned as important; no comparison with recent gradient-based QD methods

strengths: Principled theoretical contribution: Theorem 1 provides formal convergence guarantees with exponentially decaying error bounds for the approximation of MMD distances between occupancy measures
Well-motivated approach addressing a clear limitation of QD methods with occupancy measures providing a theoretically justified characterization of policy behavior
Comprehensive experimental evaluation with 5 baselines, 6 environments, multiple metrics (GT QD Score, Vendi Score, qVS), and adaptation experiments demonstrating practical benefits
Thoughtful algorithm design with calibrated weighted PCA appropriately emphasizing high-performing policies and iterative descriptor refinement
Excellent reproducibility with extensive appendices containing implementation details, hyperparameters, network architectures, and ablation studies
weaknesses: Significant theory-practice gap: Theorem 1 applies to ϕ^π from i.i.d. sampling, but the method uses ψ^π leveraging all trajectory transitions. The approximation quality of ψ^π is not theoretically analyzed

Mixed and inconsistent empirical results: AutoQD fails to consistently outperform baselines. Notably underperforms on HalfCheetah (low-performing policies despite diversity) and Walker2d (ranks second with missing behavioral variations)
Kernel width σ is fixed without justification or sensitivity analysis. Authors acknowledge this limitation but provide no solution or study of its impact on embedding quality
Limited empirical scope: Only continuous control environments from MuJoCo. No image-based observations, discrete control, or other QD application domains despite being mentioned as future work
Sample efficiency not addressed: Accurate occupancy measure estimation requires many trajectories, especially in stochastic environments. No comparison of sample complexity against baselines

Design choices appear somewhat ad-hoc: cwPCA fitness weighting scheme not compared to alternatives; 5th/95th percentile calibration lacks justification; update schedule [20, 50, 100, 200, 300] arbitrary with no ablation
Evaluation concerns: Ground-truth QD score still requires expert-designed descriptors. Separate large RFF kernel used for VS/qVS evaluation creates potential bias

strengths: Strong theoretical foundation with Theorem 1 establishing convergence of RFF embeddings to MMD distances; proof is rigorous and well-executed
Well-motivated problem using occupancy measures as complete policy characterization, providing principled alternative to proxy-based methods
Comprehensive experimental evaluation: 6 environments, 5 diverse baselines, multiple metrics (GT QD, Vendi, qVS), thorough ablations and stability analyses
Practical algorithm design: cwPCA weighting emphasizes high-performing behaviors while calibration ensures fixed archive bounds; thoughtful justification for using trajectory-based embeddings

Excellent supplementary material with implementation details, ablations, descriptor stability analysis showing AutoQD achieves orders of magnitude lower variance than baselines, and qualitative behavior visualizations
Strong results on 4/6 domains (Ant, Hopper, Swimmer, BipedalWalker) and demonstrated robustness benefits under environmental perturbations (friction, mass variations)
weaknesses: Mixed empirical results: Underperforms on HalfCheetah (diverse but low-quality) and Walker2d (suboptimal behavioral modes). Authors acknowledge early convergence to stable behaviors when k=4, but provide no principled solution—suggests systematic failure when behavioral space structure is non-obvious

Evaluation design concerns: GT QD Score uses hand-crafted descriptors (circular given method's goal), and Vendi/qVS metrics use identical RFF embeddings as AutoQD, potentially biasing evaluation. No independent diversity metrics (visual features, state distributions) provided

Limited theoretical analysis of learned descriptors: Theorem 1 bounds RFF embeddings but provides no guarantees on cwPCA projections or how descriptor updates affect QD convergence. Gap between occupancy measure theory and low-d descriptor practice not rigorously addressed

Core technical novelty is incremental: RFF approximation (Rahimi & Recht 2007), occupancy measures, and PCA are all established. Contribution is primarily integration rather than fundamental innovation

Scalability and practical concerns inadequately addressed: Method requires embedding all archived policies; tested only on simple continuous control without images/high-dimensional states. Authors acknowledge inheriting QD scalability limitations but propose no solutions. No computational cost analysis provided

Hyperparameter selection guidance lacking: Many hyperparameters (D=100, k=4, σ, update schedule) with ablations only on BipedalWalker. Kernel width σ fixed (acknowledged limitation). No principled method to select k for new domains; k=4 appears arbitrary

Sample efficiency analysis insufficient: Acknowledged that stochastic environments may require many trajectories, but no empirical demonstration. No comparison of total environment samples across methods despite this being a key practical concern

Failure mode analysis incomplete: HalfCheetah and Walker2d failures described but not systematically understood. No diagnostic method to detect when descriptor space is too constrained. Suggestion to use higher k is speculative (Figure 10 shows exponential quality degradation)

strengths: Principled theoretical framework using occupancy measures with formal convergence guarantees (Theorem 1) showing error bounds depend on sample count n and embedding dimension D
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 6 continuous control tasks with 5 strong baselines and multiple metrics (GT QD Score, Vendi Score, qVS)
Thorough documentation with detailed appendices including proofs, ablations, and qualitative behavioral analysis
Strong performance in 4/6 environments with good adaptation results to environment dynamics changes
Well-motivated use of MMD-based embeddings as alternative to hand-crafted or state-reconstruction-based behavior descriptors
weaknesses: Significant empirical failures in 2/6 environments (HalfCheetah: low quality/high diversity tradeoff; Walker2d: limited behavioral coverage) with root causes identified post-hoc but not resolved—suggests fundamental limitation rather than fixable issue
Limited core novelty: Applies existing techniques (RFF approximation from Rahimi & Recht 2007, standard PCA) to occupancy measures; the main algorithmic contribution is relatively straightforward

Substantial theory-practice gap: Theorem 1 assumes i.i.d. occupancy samples, but practical algorithm uses weighted trajectory samples (ψ^π vs ϕ^π) with different convergence properties; no empirical validation of theoretical bound tightness

Evaluation design concerns: GT QD Score uses hand-crafted descriptors misaligned with learned policies; Vendi Score uses separate RFFs inconsistent with method's internals; adaptation experiments only on 1/6 domains
Extensive hyperparameter introduction (D, k, update schedule, kernel bandwidth σ) with incomplete sensitivity analysis; update schedule never ablated; kernel bandwidth choice appears arbitrary
Scalability limitations: Only tested on low-dimensional continuous control (state dim ≤20); no image-based observations despite mentioning as future work; memory/computation complexity not analyzed

Unresolved design questions: Why does HalfCheetah discover 'sliding' policies with high diversity but poor quality? Why does Walker2d overemphasize lower joints? Post-hoc diagnoses ('early convergence') don't enable prediction or prevention

Theory assumes fully-observable MDPs and perfect occupancy measures, but practice uses finite trajectory samples; MMD captures distributional divergence but not all behavioral properties relevant to control

strengths: Strong theoretical foundation with Theorem 1 proving L2 distances between policy embeddings approximate MMD with exponential convergence in sample count and embedding dimension
Well-motivated use of occupancy measures, which provide one-to-one correspondence with policies under standard assumptions, offering principled representation of behavior
Comprehensive experimental validation across 6 continuous control environments with 5 well-chosen baselines and multiple complementary evaluation metrics (GT QD Score, Vendi Score, qVS)
Strong empirical results outperforming baselines on 5/6 environments, with particularly compelling robustness validation through environment perturbations (friction, mass scaling)

Excellent reproducibility: detailed hyperparameter specifications, clear algorithms with pseudocode, multiple random seeds, promised source code release, and extensive appendices with ablations and analysis

Thorough analysis including quality-diversity trade-off characterization (Figure 5), descriptor stability analysis (Appendix I showing orders of magnitude lower variance), and qualitative behavior visualization
Honest discussion of limitations in HalfCheetah and Walker2d with clear identification of root causes (low-dimensional descriptor bottleneck), demonstrating scientific rigor
Practical algorithm design with well-motivated calibrated weighted PCA providing stable, adaptive behavior descriptors
weaknesses: Performance limitations in 2/6 domains: HalfCheetah discovers diverse but low-quality 'sliding' behaviors; Walker2d overemphasizes lower-joint motions—root cause identified (4-d descriptor bottleneck) but suggests approach may not universally work well
Limited experimental scope restricted to continuous control with state observations; no image-based tasks or more diverse domain families; scalability to high-dimensional state/action spaces unclear

Theory-practice gap: Theorem 1 analyzes φ^π (single state-action samples) but implementation uses ψ^π (trajectory-weighted features); while Appendix B justifies this, important details are relegated to appendix rather than main text

Inherited scalability limitations from CMA-MAE dependency; method struggles with large policy networks and high-dimensional behavior spaces; performance degrades significantly with descriptor dimensionality k > 2
